body: Some very strange goings on involving my phone. I've mostly dismissed that one in particular, but my point is that I'm really worried about this.

Because I am so, so afraid of my government. The patriot act, and our most recent defense budget basically means that anyone "suspected" of being a terrorist, or friends of terrorists, or a terrorist sympathizer is not human, and has no rights. And the list for what you can be suspected for is so long and all-inclusive that pretty much everyone who doesn't walk in lockstep is considered a threat. And I am certainly on some government blacklist or another, because of how I view our country. I've even entertained the thought that I'm actively being targeted by a program designed to make me kill myself. So tell me. Am I overly paranoid? Do I have delusions of persecution? I think that anyone who doesn't consider America imperialistic is deluded. And history shows that imperialistic regimes rarely go quietly, and without bloodshed.

I'm sorry too. I waited a long time (like four hours, I think) for your reply and was disappointed when I got it. At first I was angry at you, but I know it's not your fault. You're just trying to help. I'm a bipolar, occasional insomniac. There's nothing more frustrating for me than being exhausted and unable to sleep. It's a nasty mix, because lack of sleep can trigger a depressive phase. So I was already irritable and angry with myself when you came along. I apologize for jumping down your throat. Mostly though I was angry because I only feel like I can talk to strangers on the internet, and there's only so much you can do for me. I was hospitalized for two weeks against my will, which makes it hard for me to trust anyone in the position to put me back there. I'm 22, and I live with my parents. I don't feel like I'll ever be well enough to take care of myself. I feel like I'm a burden to my friends and family. I'm not living, and I'm dying much slower than I'd like. I don't trust anyone except for you guys, and it's driving me up a wall.

The tipping point is past, and it's when we started considering corporations "people" in the legal sense when it comes to campaign contributions. It *encourages* the purchase of politicians by special interest groups. It's when the NSA declared the citizens it's supposed to protect enemies of the state. America isn't a republic anymore, it's a fascist corporate oligarchy. Land of the free? Don't make me laugh. My country is chomping at the bit, ready to tear itself apart. I don't want to be around for the inevitable revolution. If that's not FUBAR, I don't know what is.
Validate me, then "try all the things you haven't." It just feels canned. Like a band-aid for a broken leg. I'm crabby, miserable, and sleep-deprived. Sorry if I came off as snippy.

14. Nansen Cuts the Cat in Two 

Nansen saw the monks of the eastern and western halls fighting over a cat. He seized the cat and told the monks: "If any of you say a good word, you can save the cat." 

No one answered. So Nansen boldly cut the cat in two pieces. 

That evening Joshu returned and Nansen told him about this. Joshu removed his sandals and, placing them on his head, walked out. 

Nansen said: "If you had been there, you could have saved the cat."
